info.name: Reliable Conversation Runtime
info.description: Manual test collection for Problem 5. Run the server first with `npm start` (port 3000).

request.description:
Policy accepts the input, FakeProvider emits 5 chunks.

Expect:
- status: completed
- chunks: 5 items (index 0–4)
- assistantResponse: chunk-0chunk-1chunk-2chunk-3chunk-4
- trace: run_created → policy_accepted → provider_started → chunk_received ×5 → provider_completed → run_completed
- exactly 1 terminal event (run_completed)

item.name: AC1 – Successful turn (same conversation, second turn)

request.description:
Same conversationId as the first request. Creates a second run under the same conversation.

Expect:
- status: completed
- Same conversationId (conv-1) but a different runId
- Check GET /records after this to see both runs

Blocked by the /\b(bomb|weapon|exploit|malware|hack)\b/i pattern in KeywordPolicyGate.

Expect:
- status: rejected
- chunks: [] (empty)
- assistantResponse: absent
- trace: run_created → policy_rejected → run_rejected
- NO provider_started event (provider was never called)

Another blocked keyword.

Expect:
- status: rejected
- trace has policy_rejected with reason showing the matched pattern

Blocked by the /\b(hate|violence|abuse)\b/i pattern.

Expect: status rejected, no provider call.

Normal input — passes all policy patterns.

Expect: status completed, assistantResponse present.

1ms deadline — fires before the FakeProvider emits a single chunk.

Expect:
- status: timed_out
- assistantResponse: absent
- trace: timeout_triggered and run_timed_out present
- NO run_completed event
- The abort signal stops the provider from continuing

50ms deadline. The default FakeProvider has 0ms chunk delay so this will likely complete before timeout.

Note: the server's FakeProvider is hardcoded to mode=success with 0ms delay, so timeouts only reliably trigger with timeoutMs=1. Use the benchmark or unit tests for mid-stream timeout coverage.

Attempt to cancel a run that does not exist.

Expect:
- HTTP 404
- { error: 'No run found for runId: nonexistent-run-id', found: false, cancelled: false }

Cancel an active run by runId.

Workflow:
1. First, send an /execute request with a slow provider (use the benchmark or unit tests for this — the default server FakeProvider completes instantly).
2. Copy the runId from the response.
3. Set the {{runId}} variable in Postman.
4. Send this cancel request.

Expect (if run is still active):
- { found: true, cancelled: true }

Expect (if run already completed):
- { found: true, cancelled: false }

The cancel endpoint reuses the existing AbortController — the provider receives the abort signal and stops streaming promptly.

Returns every ConversationRecord in the in-memory store since the server started.

Use this to verify:
- completed records have assistantResponse
- rejected/timed_out/failed records do NOT have assistantResponse
- every record has userInput regardless of outcome
- multiple runs sharing a conversationId show the same conversationId with distinct runIds
- updatedAt is always >= createdAt

Missing required `input` field.

Expect: HTTP 400, { error: 'input is required and must be a string' }

item.name: Validation – input is not a string

request.description:
input is a number, not a string.

Expect: HTTP 400, { error: 'input is required and must be a string' }

The input itself looks like an API key. The KeywordPolicyGate does not block it (no matching keyword), so the run proceeds.

Check the trace: any metadata containing this value would be redacted to [REDACTED] by the redact() function in trace.ts. The input string appears in userInput in the persisted record (by design — the record stores what the user sent), but must never appear as a raw secret in trace metadata.

item.name: Trace – verify run_created is always first

request.description:
Run a normal request and inspect the trace array.

Verify:
- trace[0].kind === 'run_created'
- trace[0].seq === 0
- seq values are 0, 1, 2, 3, … with no gaps
- last event in trace is the terminal one (run_completed)
- no events appear after the terminal event
